_note: From NSM GP-IKT 2.1 measure to Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB) control to built-in policies. Every policy GUID comes from Microsoft's MCSB initiative (source/mcsb-<version>.json); this file only says which MCSB controls, and which of their policies, support which NSM clause. 'include' keeps only the named policyDefinitionReferenceIds of a control, 'exclude' drops the named ones, neither means the whole control. strength: direkte = the setting is what the clause asks for; delvis = evidence for the clause within the stated scope, or Microsoft's check is stricter or narrower than NSM's wording. Weak links are left out and listed under left_out. 'scope' is shown in coverage.md and in the initiative's metadata, in Norwegian.

links.scope: Virtuelle nettverk og virtuelle maskiner i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: NSM asks for zones and names 'virtualiserte nett' and 'mikrosegmentering'; a network security group on every subnet and machine shows each sits behind a zone boundary, not that the zone model fits the risk profile.

links.scope: PaaS-tjenester i Azure som kan plasseres i virtuelt nettverk, i tildelt omfang
links.why: Placing a platform service inside a virtual network puts it in one of the organisation's zones instead of on the public network.

links.scope: Azure- og Arc-maskiner i tildelt omfang
links.why: 'Installer sikkerhetsoppdateringer så fort som mulig' and d) 'automatisere': machines check for missing updates on a schedule and have none outstanding.

links.scope: Azure Machine Learning-instanser i tildelt omfang
links.why: Compute instances get security updates only when they are recreated on the latest image.

links.scope: App Service og Functions i tildelt omfang
links.why: i) 'eldre eller ubrukte protokoller': old TLS versions are switched off.

links.scope: App Service, Functions, Azure SQL, API Management og Windows-servere i tildelt omfang
links.why: i) 'eldre eller ubrukte protokoller': plain FTP, old TLS versions and unencrypted API protocols are switched off.

links.scope: App Service og Functions i tildelt omfang
links.why: iii) 'andre innebygde tjenester virksomheten ikke kommer til å benytte': remote debugging is a built-in service that production apps do not need.

links.scope: Windows- og Linux-servere i Azure og Arc, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) one centralised standard per type of unit: the servers meet the Azure compute security baseline. It counts as NSM's standard only if the organisation has adopted that baseline for its servers.

links.scope: Windows- og Linux-servere i Azure og Arc, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) 'sammenlign regelmessig aktivert konfigurasjon ... mot den godkjente' and d) 'automatiser': machine configuration compares each server with the baseline continuously. The approved configuration here is Microsoft's baseline, and clients, firewalls and network equipment are outside.

links.scope: Virtuelle maskiner i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) ii) 'unngå å eksponere administrative grensesnitt på internett': management ports are closed, or opened only on request for a limited time.

links.scope: API Management i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) ii): the direct management endpoint of API Management is an administrative interface that should not be exposed.

links.scope: Linux-maskiner i Azure og Arc, i tildelt omfang
links.why: 'redusere mulighet for passordbasert autentisering over nettverket': Linux machines accept SSH keys only. It says nothing about default passwords on other products.

links.scope: Virtuelle maskiner i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) only allow-listed traffic between zones and towards the internet: network security groups do not leave all ports open.

links.scope: Virtuelle maskiner og virtuelle nettverk i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) traffic towards the internet passes the organisation's firewall, and machines do not route traffic around it.

links.scope: PaaS-tjenester i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) filter traffic by allow-list: the services' own firewalls restrict who can reach them. Several of Microsoft's checks ask for public access to be closed altogether, which is stricter than NSM's wording, so a deviation needs judgement.

links.scope: Nettsteder bak Application Gateway og Front Door, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) 'Eksponerte tjenester som web ... bør kontrolleres spesielt': a web application firewall inspects traffic to exposed web services. Clause b, no direct flow to the most critical services, is not measured.

links.scope: Kubernetes-tjenester, Key Vault og API Management i tildelt omfang
links.why: b) 'minste privilegiums prinsipp': role-based access is switched on, so access can be granted per role instead of all or nothing. It shows least privilege is possible there, not that every grant is minimal.

links.scope: Datatjenester, lagring og VPN i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) manage accounts for as many resources as possible with one tool: the services accept only Entra ID identities, so no local accounts or shared keys live outside the directory.

links.scope: Azure Database for MySQL i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) as for the other data services: MySQL servers authenticate with Entra ID. Microsoft files these two policies under encryption at rest; by content they are about authentication.

links.scope: Rolletildelinger i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: d) follow up accounts that are no longer needed: blocked accounts hold no roles on Azure resources. Accounts that are enabled but unused are not found by these policies.

links.scope: Eier-rollen på abonnementer i tildelt omfang
links.why: b) limit accounts with full rights to a minimum: at most three owners per subscription. Owner is the Azure role with full rights.

links.scope: Key Vault i tildelt omfang
links.why: The strategy should cover 'fornyelse av nøkler': keys and secrets carry an expiry date. Evidence that this part of a strategy is practised in Key Vault; the strategy itself is attested.

links.scope: Key Vault i tildelt omfang
links.why: The strategy should cover 'håndtering av sertifikater': certificates have a maximum validity period.

links.scope: Key Vault i tildelt omfang
links.why: The strategy should cover 'hvordan nøkler/passord oppbevares' and 'sikkerhetskopiering av nøkler': deleted keys can be recovered and cannot be purged.

links.scope: Disker, databaser og tjenester i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: 'Aktiver kryptering i de tjenestene som tilbyr slik funksjonalitet': encryption at rest is switched on where the service offers it.

links.scope: Tjenester i Azure med nettverksendepunkt, i tildelt omfang
links.why: 'Aktiver kryptering ...' and 'kun anbefalte algoritmer': the services require TLS, in a current version.

links.scope: Tjenester i Azure med nettverksendepunkt, i tildelt omfang
links.why: 'Benytt kryptering når konfidensiell informasjon overføres', with TLS in the application as NSM's own example: the services refuse unencrypted connections.

links.scope: Virtuelle maskiner i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: The measure is a plan; a) says which data to back up. Azure Backup on every virtual machine shows the plan is carried out for those machines, never the plan itself.

links.scope: Virtuelle maskiner og SQL i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: 'jevnlig sårbarhetskartlegging ... ved hjelp av automatiserte verktøy': a vulnerability assessment tool is switched on. NSM also names clients and network, which are outside.

links.scope: SQL og containeravbildninger i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) 'verifiser at oppdagede sårbarheter blir håndtert': findings from the assessments are resolved.

links.scope: Servere i Azure og Arc, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) centrally managed anti-malware: Defender for Servers is on, which brings Defender for Endpoint to the servers.

links.scope: Windows-servere i Azure og Arc, i tildelt omfang
links.why: b) 'IDS/IPS-funksjonalitet på klienter og servere': Exploit Guard, the host intrusion prevention in Windows, is on.

links.scope: Databaser, lagring, Key Vault, App Service, containere og Resource Manager i Azure, i tildelt omfang
links.why: a) the parts that are most critical or hold the most confidential information: threat detection is on for these resource types. It shows they are monitored, not that the organisation has decided what to monitor.

links.scope: Tjenester i Azure med ressurslogger, i tildelt omfang
links.why: b) 'administrasjons- og sikkerhetslogger fra enheter og tjenester': resource logs and SQL auditing are switched on. The decision on which data is relevant is attested, and sign-in logs (a) come from Entra ID, not from Azure Policy.

left_out.why: Retired resource types and unused APIs. Closest NSM text is 2.1.2 c) 'eldre IKT-produkter fases ut', which is about purchasing; a candidate if 2.1.2 is to be measured in Azure.
Geo-redundancy protects against loss of a region. NSM 2.9.4 asks for copies separated from production and for offline copies, which it does not show. BR-2 holds the same four policies as BR-1.
Defender plans; the same policies are counted once under 3.2.3 through LT-1.
Customer-managed keys. NSM 2.7.1 asks for a strategy; an organisation whose strategy uses platform-managed keys would be marked as deviating.

left_out.mcsb: DP-6 (API Management named values), DP-8 (logs, Defender, firewall, private link)
left_out.why: Counted under other measures or not about key handling.
Its two policies are counted under 3.1.1 through PV-6.
Managed identities, API authentication and secrets found on machines. No NSM clause names them closely enough.
MCSB no longer carries the policies for MFA on subscription accounts. MFA for Azure is decided in Entra ID Conditional Access and is measured by the Maester pack (MP.NSM.1005).
Incident contacts and alert quality. NSM 4.1 is planning and exercises, which are attested.
Retention of SQL audit logs. NSM 3.2.5 b) is about storage space and 3.2.6 about tampering; neither is retention.

left_out.mcsb: NS-2 (private link policies, anonymous blob access, MariaDB)
left_out.why: Private link is one way to meet 2.5.1, not something NSM asks for: a service with a firewall allow-list would be marked as deviating. Anonymous blob access is about authorisation, not network. Azure Database for MariaDB is retired.
DDoS protection. NSM mentions denial of service only as a topic for risk assessment in 2.2.7.

left_out.mcsb: PA-1 (more than one owner; blocked and guest owners), PA-4 (guest accounts)
left_out.why: More than one owner is about availability. NSM does not ask for guests to be removed; a guest with a role is a deviation only by Microsoft's rule.
Its one policy, just-in-time access to management ports, is counted under 2.3.6 through NS-3.
Flags every custom role, which NSM does not advise against.

left_out.mcsb: PV-2 (Kubernetes pod security, CORS, API Management platform version)
left_out.why: NSM 2.3.4 names operating systems, firewalls, network equipment, applications and hardware. Kubernetes workload rules need the organisation's own allow-lists; candidates once it has a Kubernetes standard.

left_out.mcsb: PV-4 (trusted launch, guest attestation, Azure Stack HCI)
left_out.why: Hardware-rooted boot protection is not named in NSM 2.3.4 or 2.3.5. The application control policy for Azure Stack HCI is about servers; NSM 2.3.2 says clients.
Secrets on disk are not vulnerability mapping.

not_in_azure_policy: NSM 2.3.2, 2.4.4, 2.6.4, 2.6.7, 2.7.3 and the governance measures have no policy here: they are measured on clients and in Entra ID by the NSM GP-IKT 2.1 [Maester pack](https://github.com/alventech/maester-pack-nsm-gp-ikt), or attested.
